recipes.description: A pre-war hand-crank gramophone. The lacquer is cracked but the mechanism still turns.
recipes.restoration_text: The gramophone crackles to life. A scratchy recording of a string quartet fills the bunker. For three minutes and forty seconds, everyone stops what they're doing and just listens.

recipes.description: A portable film projector, bulb intact but mechanism seized from decades of disuse.
recipes.restoration_text: The projector whirs to life, casting flickering images on the bunker wall. It's an old home movie — a birthday party, a child blowing out candles. No one knows these people. Everyone watches anyway.

recipes.description: A vacuum-tube ham radio transceiver, pre-digital, built to last through anything.
recipes.restoration_text: The radio hums with static, then — a voice. Faint, distant, but unmistakably human. 'Hello? Is anyone out there?' The bunker holds its breath.

recipes.description: A small silver music box, tarnished but intact. The winding key is still attached.
recipes.restoration_text: The music box plays a melody no one recognizes but everyone feels. An old lullaby, maybe. A child hums along, and for just a moment, the bunker feels like a home.

recipes.description: A heavy cast-iron typewriter. The ribbon is dry but the keys still strike true.
recipes.restoration_text: The typewriter's clack fills the quiet hours. Survivors take turns typing letters — to loved ones, to the future, to no one in particular. The paper stacks up like a testament.

recipes.description: A medium-format camera, lenses fogged but body solid. The shutter still clicks.
recipes.restoration_text: The camera captures the bunker in black and white — tired faces, patched walls, small kindnesses. Someone suggests a group portrait. For the first time since the exchange, everyone smiles at once.
